findings.status: Still structurally true; retained scheduler limitation, not a new regression
findings.evidence: One start_worker jthread synchronously executes at most a fixture lease, a read lease, a map lease and a persistent-search lease per iteration before its 20 ms sleep. A synchronous read RPC delays advancement of that shared background dispatcher.
findings.limits: The read grant is capped at 55,000 ms with a 5,000 ms RPC allowance. This does not prove a specific delay occurred, and foreground HTTP calls use a different path; do not claim every request is blocked by one background read.
findings.disposition: Not changed in this specified repair batch; this is retained early-review evidence, not a fresh runtime or load test.

findings.status: Still structurally true; retained HTTP executor capacity limitation
findings.evidence: Session::received calls service_.dispatch synchronously on the bounded IO pool (default 8). HttpWorker::call synchronously runs its own RPC io_context. The web.read maximum 60,000 ms plus 5,000 ms RPC allowance can occupy those outer IO threads.
findings.limits: The /healthz business path is fast and avoids Store/auth work, but it has no reserved executor. Saturating every IO thread can delay health; a single slow request with spare threads need not do so. No load reproduction was run here.
findings.disposition: Not changed in this specified repair batch; this is retained early-review evidence, not a fresh runtime or load test.

findings.status: Quarantined restore boundary remains intentional; audit wording overstates it
findings.evidence: backup.create performs an actual complete SQLite backup into a closed, quarantined artifact and atomically publishes it without overwrite. Normal Store opening refuses quarantine. There is no supported product restore/reconciliation-to-serving command.
findings.correction: Backup artifacts exist. Safe restoration to a serving instance remains unimplemented and intentionally fail-closed; this is not equivalent to no backup, nor proof that restoration can never be implemented.
findings.disposition: Not changed in this specified repair batch; this is retained early-review evidence, not a fresh runtime or load test.
findings.delivery_note: A real isolated SQLite backup exists. The missing capability is a supported restore/reconciliation-to-serving workflow; backup isolation remains unchanged.

findings.status: Very long upstream cooldown is accepted and persisted; not a manifest disable
findings.evidence: Retry-After is bounded only by (1<<62)-1 ms. Core takes the maximum of its configured cooldown and the upstream value; source_report stores MAX(existing cooldown_until, new until). Source admission checks it across restarts. A late success does not clear the cooldown.
findings.limits: This can make a budget key unavailable for roughly 31.7 years, but does not change source enabled/review state. It may apply to sources sharing that key. No live source was requested; default source disabling remains intact.
findings.disposition: Not changed in this specified repair batch; this is retained early-review evidence, not a fresh runtime or load test.
findings.delivery_note: No 24-hour Retry-After cap was implemented because P2-9 is outside the specified fixes for this batch. This index does not impose additional user approval or identify such approval as one of the six retained decisions.
